answer: Require each agent identity to stake a small deposit as a kernel of trust before it can transact. Every interaction then emits a verifiable signal — a signed receipt — that peers attach to the sender's vertex in the shared reputation graph. A sybil farm must fund a fresh kernel for every fake vertex and generate real, costly interactions to build any signal, so faking thousands of convincing identities costs thousands of deposits plus sustained work, while an honest agent reuses one cheap, long-lived identity.
